trans.sense: (medicine) initial phase of a disease or condition

examples.text: In mild cases of hypergonadism prior to puberty, the onset of physical and mood changes may not be abnormally early or significant enough to cause any psychological or long-term physical complications.

examples.text: The only regular sources for Sardinian *θ are Lat. ci̯ and ti̯, which are absent from Latin onsets. This means that the substantial number of words starting in *θ, discussed in § 3 – 7, cannot regularly continue a Latin form.

glosses: The initial portion of a syllable, preceding the syllable nucleus.

raw_glosses: (acoustics) The beginning of a musical note or other sound, in which the amplitude rises from zero to an initial peak.
glosses: The beginning of a musical note or other sound, in which the amplitude rises from zero to an initial peak.

examples.text: There is surely no greater wisdom than well to time the beginnings and onsets of things.

examples.text: Floods in northern India, mostly in the small state of Uttarakhand, have wrought disaster on an enormous scale. The early, intense onset of the monsoon on June 14th swelled rivers, washing away roads, bridges, hotels and even whole villages. Rock-filled torrents smashed vehicles and homes, burying victims under rubble and sludge.
